the dense gas traced by the CS J =5 → 4 emission is very dense, but much less dense than would be predicted from the critical density of this line.
the dense gas associated with star formation is very dense and very massive, and is not in virial equilibrium.

the gas is dense, but not as dense as expected; the star formation efficiency in the dense gas is very high, but not as high as expected; the depletion time for the gas is comparable to the timescales for gas dispersal in the Galaxy; and the luminosity in the CS line is much less than that in the central regions of M82 and NGC 253

the dense gas in the Galactic disk is not as dense or massive as that seen in the nuclei of nearby galaxies.
